title: optimizer-safety-playbook-and-graceful-revert-guidelines
creator: Maya Patel
description: Goal: Deliver an operator-friendly, low-risk playbook for the Optimize autotuner that enforces safe config application, deterministic rollback, and cost-regression detection for batching/caching rules. Scope: recommendations engine (rules + thresholds), preflight checks, canary rollout policy, automated revert with audit trail, and post-deploy monitoring hooks. Out of scope: scheduler kernel changes, hardware-level kernel switchover. Success metrics: mean rollback time < 5 minutes, zero customer-facing error increase post-rollback, cost-per-token reduction preserved >= 8% on measured job cohorts, zero unplanned data exposure. This ticket consolidates incident findings, formalizes mitigations, and implements the minimal automation to prevent recurrence.
postmortem_summary: On 2026-01-28 a scheduled Optimize autotuner rollout changed batching thresholds and aggressive KV cache expiration simultaneously. The combined change increased short-tail latency (P95) by 2.6x for small prompt workloads and caused KV cache thrashing on dedicated pools. Operator attempts to revert were delayed because the rollout applied at regional granularity without an emergency toggle and the revert path required manual coordination across three services. Root causes: (1) lack of preflight simulation covering sequence length distribution; (2) no staged canary policy for cache-expiry changes; (3) insufficient visibility into per-route token composition. Impact: latency SLO breaches for several customers, transient 22% cost spike on affected pools, and two support tickets. No customer data was exposed.
mitigations: Implement preflight simulation that replays representative traffic over candidate batching/caching configs
Introduce per-change feature flags and an emergency global rollback toggle in the Console
Require staged canaries: 0.5% traffic -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with automated health gates
Add a guardrail that prevents simultaneous batching and cache-expiry policy changes in a single rollout
Add per-route cost and latency assertions with automatic rollback if thresholds are exceeded
Retention of full KV cache telemetry for 72 hours post-change to diagnose thrash quickly
Documented operator runbook with step-by-step revert and validation commands
playbook_summary: Operator playbook (high level): 1) Before apply: run 'optimize-sim' against a maintained traffic snapshot; ensure simulated P95 delta < +10% and cost delta <= target. 2) Deploy: push change behind feature flag and start canary at 0.5% for 20 minutes. 3) Monitor: automatic checks for latency, error-rate, token-cost, and cache-hit-rate; enforce gates. 4) On violation: trigger automated revert via the Console toggle which restores previous config atomically and re-provisions cache warmers for 10 minutes. 5) Post-mortem: collect traces, KV cache metrics, and cost deltas; tag release with 'safety-reviewed' and require a secondary approval to reapply. Playbook includes command-line snippets and pre-defined dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Preflight simulation merged and run in CI for every optimizer change
Console exposes emergency rollback toggle that reverts configs within 120s operationally (target < 300s for full restoration)
Canary gates implemented and configurable per-release
Automated alerts and rollback are tested in a synthetic canary job in staging and documented
Operator runbook and Confluence page published and reviewed by SRE/Product/DevRel
